title: Voltpilot MQTT Schedule Payload
description: Battery dispatch plan published by the cloud optimizer (services/optimization) on ems/{tenant_id}/{site_id}/{device_id}/schedule as a RETAINED QoS1 message, so a (re)connecting edge always receives the current plan immediately. This is a BINDING contract (architecture section 20 item 8). The shape deliberately adopts what the Node-RED schedule-exec flow already consumed (slot_minutes + slots[].start/battery_setpoint_kw) and adds plan metadata for traceability; the edge ignores fields it does not need.
x-failsafe: The plan is ADVISORY: the edge clamps every commanded setpoint through its local Guards (charge/discharge limits, SoC bounds, the observed §14a envelope) before any register write. When the retained schedule is missing, malformed, or stale (no fresh schedule received for 20 minutes - the edge Default-Watchdog window), or when 'now' falls outside every slot, the edge falls back to the self-consumption default (battery follows PV - load). The optimizer republishes well inside the staleness window (every 15 minutes), so the fallback only engages on a real outage.

plan_id.description: Unique id of this optimization run; keys the persisted plan (schedule hypertable) for plan-vs-actual evaluation.

generated_at.description: When the optimizer produced this plan (RFC 3339, UTC).

horizon_slots.description: Number of slots in the plan (96 = 24h at 15 min). Redundant with slots.length; carried for cheap introspection.

slot_minutes.description: Slot width in minutes. v1 always publishes 15 (the platform-wide optimization grid); the field exists so the edge never has to assume.

grid_charge_allowed.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07, P5 EEG execution gap; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working unchanged). Mirrors site.netzladen_erlaubt at plan time. false = the plant is EEG-funded (Ausschliesslichkeitsprinzip): the edge MUST clamp any commanded battery CHARGE to max(measured_pv, 0) before a register write - PV-bus Bilanzierung (FK3, captain decision 2026-07-16): the battery may charge up to the full ACTUAL PV production while the house draws its load from the grid in parallel (DC-hybrid physics); measured PV is the inverter's actual output (already post-curtailment), making this the on-device twin of the optimizer's charge <= pv - curtail constraint, applied to MEASURED values so a PV forecast overshoot can never turn a planned solar charge into real grid import. Unknown/missing PV reading clamps charge to 0 (never charge blind). true = grid charging is permitted (merchant mode), no extra clamp. ABSENT = treat as allowed (pre-P5 behavior; a legacy payload must not suddenly clamp a merchant site - the optimizer always publishes the field, so absence only occurs from an old cloud, where the edge behaves exactly as before). Discharge is never affected. SAFETY: this field can only ever RESTRICT charging, never widen any other guard.

grid_import_limit_kw.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07, PS-1 peak shaving / Lastspitzenkappung; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working unchanged, which IS the failsafe for old edge builds). The run's planned billing-period peak target in kW: the highest 15-min mean grid IMPORT the optimizer planned for (the solved peak-epigraph variable, >= the period's measured peak so far). Present ONLY while the site's peak-shaving module is active (site.leistungspreis_eur_kw configured); absent = no peak module - an edge MUST treat absent/unknown as 'no import target', and a NEW plan without the field MUST clear any previously applied peak-guard target. STALENESS (amended 2026-07 with PS-3, superseding the original clear-on-stale reading): the billing peak is a 15-min MEAN only the edge can defend in closed loop, so on a STALE schedule the edge KEEPS defending the LAST plan-carried target inside its self-consumption fallback (first hold the target, ordinary discharge only down to peak_reserve_soc_pct) - deliberately safe because the guard is restrict-only (raise discharge / reduce charge, inside every compliance clamp), so a dead optimizer's target can never widen anything; it can only save Leistungspreis money. The target is ADVISORY like every setpoint: the edge-side peak guard (PS-3) discharges against a forming 15-min import peak up to its guard-clamped limits - it never widens any battery/SoC/§14a guard, and never curtails load. Import-side ONLY: export is never affected.
grid_import_limit_kw.x-failsafe: Absent field (or a new plan without it) => no peak-guard target (clear any latch). Stale schedule => the edge keeps defending the last known target (PS-3; restrict-only, so never a safety concern) while the setpoint falls back to reserve-floored self-consumption. No grid measurement => the guard is inactive (never regulate blind). The Leistungspreis economics are re-anchored by the cloud every 15 min from measured rollups, so a missed window only costs money, never safety.

grid_export_limit_kw.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-08-06, dynamische Einspeisebegrenzung am Netzverknuepfungspunkt; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working exactly as before, which IS the failsafe for old edge builds). The site's STATIC feed-in limit at the grid connection point in kW (site.max_feed_in_kw, the Excel reference spec's 'Max Einspeisung am Netzpunkt' - the same master datum the optimizer already applies as a hard EXPORT cap, FK1). It is the EXPORT-side twin of grid_import_limit_kw and exists because a 15-min plan cannot hold a connection-point limit: the limit is shared with the house, so unplugging a wallbox raises the feed-in by that wallbox's power WITHIN the slot (measured at Anlage Pilsting, where a customer-owned Loxone did this job: 'sonst schiesst der drueber wenn ein Auto abgesteckt wird'). The edge therefore runs a REAL-TIME watchdog (guards.ExportLimiter) that regulates the site's CONTROLLABLE producers against the MEASURED grid power - house load, wallboxes and battery are netted in automatically because they are already inside that measurement - and hands the resulting plant-level PV cap to the existing curtailment executor. COMPOSITION: most restrictive wins with the per-slot pv_limit_kw (planned curtailment); the watchdog can only ever REDUCE generation and never widens a planned curtailment, a §14a envelope or any battery guard. SCOPE: the battery is NEVER a means of enforcement here (absorbing a surplus is an optimizer decision, per-slot charge_surplus_to_battery) - only the controllable producers are regulated. Present only when the site has the limit configured; absent = no feed-in limit - an edge MUST treat absent/unknown as 'no limit' and MUST clear any previously applied watchdog target when a NEW plan omits the field. A limit is never invented.
grid_export_limit_kw.x-failsafe: Absent field (or a new plan without it) => no watchdog target (clear any latch); the plan's own pv_limit_kw curtailment continues to apply unchanged. STALE schedule => the edge KEEPS regulating against the LAST known limit (like grid_import_limit_kw, and here the argument is stronger: a dead optimizer must never hand a plant back its unlimited feed-in; the watchdog is restrict-only, so a stale limit can only cost yield, never safety). ⚠ MEASUREMENT LOSS IS THE ONE PLACE WHERE THIS FIELD'S FAILSAFE IS THE OPPOSITE OF EVERY OTHER GUARD'S: the economic guards go INACTIVE when blind ('never regulate blind'), but for a compliance limit 'blind' must not mean 'unlimited'. The edge therefore degrades in stages instead of releasing - it HOLDS the last commanded cap through a short measurement gap, then CONTRACTS gradually to a safe static cap (limit minus the commanded battery discharge, which holds for ANY house load because export = pv + discharge - load - charge <= pv + discharge), and adopts that safe cap immediately when it has never measured at all. ENFORCEABILITY IS NOT ASSUMED: the cap is only written to inverters the operator released per unit (First-Light) while the control kill-switch is on; where nothing can be written the edge says so loudly on its local page and in its status heartbeat rather than implying a protection it does not provide, and generation the edge cannot command (an uncertified or non-curtailable inverter) is accounted for but cannot be held back.

peak_reserve_soc_pct.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07, PS-2 peak-shaving reserve; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0). Mirrors site.peak_reserve_soc_pct: the SoC floor (percent of capacity) reserved for peak shaving, so the edge's OWN fallback (self-consumption on a dead cloud link) can stop discharging ordinary load at this floor and keep the reserve for a real peak. Consumed by the PS-3 edge guard: in the stale-plan fallback, ordinary self-consumption discharge stops at this floor while peak DEFENSE (holding grid_import_limit_kw) may still discharge below it, down to the technical SoC floor - that is what the reserve is FOR. Present only alongside grid_import_limit_kw (module active) and only when the reserve is configured. SAFETY: this field can only ever RESTRICT discharge (raise a floor), never widen any guard; an edge without support ignores it safely.

effective_floor_soc_pct.description: OPTIONAL additive execution floor for corrective discharge: max(technical SoC floor, customer backup reserve, peak reserve). A new edge MUST require this field before STARTING discharge from an idle slot; absent/invalid therefore disables unplanned_load_discharge. Old edges ignore it safely.

slots.description: Contiguous 15-min slots in ascending start order, covering at least the next 24h at publish time. The edge executes the slot whose [start, start+slot_minutes) contains 'now'.

start.description: Slot start (RFC 3339, UTC), aligned to the slot grid.

battery_setpoint_kw.description: Target mean battery power over the slot. Signed: positive = charge, negative = discharge. Advisory - the edge Guards clamp it.

pv_limit_kw.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07, Phase 3 negative-price curtailment; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working unchanged). Maximum PV active power over the slot, kW, >= 0: the inverter feed-in cap implementing planned curtailment (the optimizer sets it to forecast PV minus planned curtailment, so it also caps forecast overshoot). Absent = no curtailment, the inverter free-runs - an edge MUST treat absent/unknown as 'no limit' and MUST clear any previously applied limit when the field is absent, when the schedule goes stale (x-failsafe), or on fallback. SAFETY: this field can only ever REDUCE generation - never a negative value, never a command to produce, and it MUST NOT affect battery safety caps; the edge Guards re-clamp it to [0, inf) before any register write.

charge_from_surplus_only.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07-30, price-aware in-slot trim; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working exactly as before). true = in THIS slot the cloud has determined that topping the battery up from the grid is UNECONOMIC: the import price of the slot exceeds what one more stored kWh earns over the rest of the horizon (the optimizer's own marginal value of stored energy, discounted by one-way efficiency and battery wear - see services/optimization/voltpilot_optimization/slot_trim.py). The edge MUST then clamp commanded battery CHARGE to the MEASURED surplus max(pv - load, 0) at the connection point, so a forecast deviation inside the quarter hour (a cloud, a load step) can no longer be covered by silently buying expensive grid energy for the battery. THE PRICE DECISION STAYS IN THE CLOUD: the edge never evaluates a price, it only enforces this flag. Distinct from (and composing with) the top-level grid_charge_allowed: that one is REGULATORY (EEG Ausschliesslichkeitsprinzip, charge <= measured PV production, the house may import in parallel), this one is ECONOMIC (charge <= measured PV SURPLUS, so the battery causes no import at all). Most restrictive wins; neither can ever widen anything. ABSENT or false = no economic restriction, i.e. exactly the pre-2026-07-30 behavior. Absence is deliberately FAIL-OPEN (unlike grid_charge_allowed, which the Go edge fails SAFE on): a missing economic hint must never change dispatch, and an unpriced restriction on a merchant site would destroy real arbitrage. The optimizer sets it only on slots whose plan actually commands a CHARGE, so every other payload stays byte-identical.
charge_from_surplus_only.x-failsafe: Absent field / false / no active slot / STALE schedule => no trim (the self-consumption fallback follows pv - load and never grid-charges anyway, so the flag is a no-op there). Unknown pv or load measurement => the trim stays INACTIVE (never regulate blind - the economic-guard convention, like the PS-3 peak guard). The trim only ever LOWERS commanded charge toward the measured surplus, so the resulting predicted grid power is max(load - pv, 0) >= 0: it can never push the site into export and therefore never re-violates the §14a export bound or a feed-in cap, and the import bound was applied to a value it only reduces further. Discharge is never affected. A trim is a DELIBERATE limitation, not a failed write: the edge writes the trimmed value, so the register readback matches it and the confirmation logic must never report 'setpoint not adopted'.

cover_load_from_battery.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07-30, in-slot load following - the DISCHARGE-side mirror of charge_from_surplus_only; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working exactly as before). true = in THIS slot the cloud has determined that covering the house from the battery is ECONOMIC: the import price of the slot exceeds what the discharged kWh costs, i.e. the optimizer's own marginal value of stored energy raised by one-way efficiency plus battery wear (import_price > lambda/eta + wear + margin - see services/optimization/voltpilot_optimization/slot_trim.py). The edge MUST then TRACK commanded battery DISCHARGE to the MEASURED deficit max(load - pv, 0) at the connection point - i.e. steer the slot toward grid power = 0 in BOTH directions: RAISE a discharge that falls short of the measured deficit AND LIMIT one that exceeds it, with a hard floor at zero discharge (the edge never commands a charge and never flips the direction) - instead of executing the slot's forecast-derived watt value rigidly and settling the difference at the grid. THE PRICE DECISION STAYS IN THE CLOUD: the edge never evaluates a price, it only enforces this flag against measured values. WHY IT IS NEEDED: a 15-min setpoint stands for the whole quarter hour, but the house load moves every second, and the load FORECAST that produced the setpoint is a quarter-hour estimate - so the forecast error is settled at the grid in whichever direction it points. BOTH halves were measured at Anlage Pilsting on 2026-07-30: at 21:22 a forecast of 4.33 kW against a measured 7.12 kW house, so the 2.79 kW difference was BOUGHT at ~32.5 ct while the battery sat at 77 % SoC; at 23:12 the mirror image, 6.7 kW planned into a 5.1 kW house, so 1.4 kW was EXPORTED at ~21 ct while that same kWh was worth ~32.5 ct as avoided import a few hours later. ABSENT or false = no load following, i.e. exactly the pre-2026-07-30 behavior. Absence is deliberately FAIL-OPEN, exactly like charge_from_surplus_only: an unpriced hint must never reshape dispatch, and inferring the duty would turn the price-aware plan back into the price-blind self-consumption logic. EMISSION: the optimizer sets it only on slots whose plan actually commands a DISCHARGE and plans NO grid exchange worth the name - |grid_kw| <= 0.05 kW, the 'grid ~ 0' kink of the eigenverbrauch role. BOTH sides are excluded on purpose: a planned IMPORT is a deliberate cheap-hour purchase the edge must never undo, and a planned EXPORT is a deliberate sale that the bidirectional enforcement above would otherwise cut back to zero grid - the edge cannot tell an intended export from a forecast overshoot (it receives only the setpoint, never the plan's own forecast grid power), so the distinction is made in the cloud, where both numbers exist. Every other payload therefore stays byte-identical and deliberate price arbitrage is untouched in BOTH directions.
cover_load_from_battery.x-failsafe: Absent field / false / no active slot / STALE schedule => no load following (the self-consumption fallback already follows pv - load, so the flag is a no-op there by construction). Unknown pv or load measurement => INACTIVE (never regulate blind - the economic-guard convention, like the PS-3 peak guard and the trim). SAFETY BY ALGEBRA: the duty only ever moves the predicted grid power (load + battery - pv) TOWARD zero - never past it, never further away - so it can neither push the site into export (the §14a export bound and any feed-in cap stay valid on the value that entered it) nor raise the import above what entered it (same for the import bound). Where it bites it lands where the BATTERY stops contributing: exactly 0 whenever the house has a deficit, and the remaining PV surplus where it has none (absorbing that would need a CHARGE, which this duty must never command). A RAISED discharge is bounded by the rated discharge power and stops at the SoC floor - and at a peak_reserve_soc_pct reserve, which exists precisely so ordinary load covering does not eat it; a LIMITED one needs no bound of its own (it shrinks the discharge magnitude and stops at zero, so rated band, SoC floor, SoC ceiling and the EEG solar-only charge clamp all hold trivially) and is never held back by the reserve, which it only ever preserves. A commanded CHARGE is never touched. Load following is a DELIBERATE correction IN EITHER DIRECTION, not a failed write: the edge writes the followed value, so the register readback matches it and the confirmation logic must never report 'setpoint not adopted' - the edge names the direction on its local card instead.

unplanned_load_discharge.description: OPTIONAL additive idle-slot authorization. true means the cloud's full marginal economics authorize covering an unforeseen measured house deficit from a planned 0-kW hold slot. It does NOT redefine cover_load_from_battery. The edge may act only with fresh known load, PV and SoC, a valid effective_floor_soc_pct, no E-stop/First-Light conflict, and must target max(load-pv,0) without battery export. Planned charge and discharge slots are never marked; a slot whose own FORECAST exports is no longer excluded (2026-08-28) - in an idle slot the export is PV, never a battery sale, and the edge caps the correction at the MEASURED deficit, so it bites only where reality imports. Native charge-block/autonomous-discharge is permitted only for an exact certified model/firmware capability; every other inverter uses the guarded exact-setpoint LoadFollower. Absent/false/stale plan fails closed.

charge_surplus_to_battery.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-08-02, in-slot surplus absorption - the CHARGE-side counterpart that RAISES a commanded charge, completing the pair with charge_from_surplus_only, which only ever LOWERS one; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working exactly as before). true = in THIS slot the cloud has determined that STORING one more kWh beats SELLING it: the marginal value of a stored kWh (the optimizer's own water value, discounted by one-way efficiency and battery wear: eta*lambda - wear) exceeds the slot's export value by the decision margin - see services/optimization/voltpilot_optimization/slot_trim.py. The edge MUST then RAISE the commanded battery CHARGE to the MEASURED surplus max(pv - load, 0) at the connection point, so a PV surplus the 15-min forecast did not see is stored instead of being exported (or, at a negative price, paid to give away). THE PRICE DECISION STAYS IN THE CLOUD: the edge never evaluates a price, it only enforces this flag against measured values. WHY IT IS NEEDED: the solver charges only the FORECAST surplus (charge <= pv_forecast - curtail), so an under-forecast PV morning plans 0.0 kW charge and every 15-min re-plan repeats it - measured at Anlage Pilsting on 2026-08-02, where a plant at 7 % SoC exported 16,6 kW at a negative price for hours while the plan curtailed on paper. ABSENT or false = no absorption duty, i.e. exactly the pre-2026-08-02 behavior. Absence is deliberately FAIL-OPEN, exactly like its two siblings: an unpriced hint must never reshape dispatch, and inferring the duty would be the price-blind self-consumption logic the price-aware plan replaced. EMISSION: the optimizer sets it only on slots where storing beats selling AND the plan itself intends no deliberate SALE (grid_kw >= -0.05 kW - or a curtailing slot, which by definition prefers not to export) AND the plan's own SoC trajectory still has headroom (an unfulfillable duty is never published). A planned IMPORT is NOT excluded, unlike cover_load_from_battery: this duty is UNIDIRECTIONAL (it only RAISES a charge, and only up to the measured surplus, i.e. up to predicted grid 0), so it bites only where reality is EXPORTING and can never touch a deliberate cheap-hour purchase - which by construction charges MORE than the surplus. That matters because under FK3 PV-bus semantics an EEG plant legitimately plans 'battery takes the PV, house takes its load from the grid', so an ordinary charging slot plans grid_kw = +load. COMPOSITION: most restrictive wins with the top-level grid_charge_allowed - the EEG clamp (charge <= measured PV production) and every other guard still apply on top, and the duty can never widen any of them.
charge_surplus_to_battery.x-failsafe: Absent field / false / no active slot / STALE schedule => no absorption (the self-consumption fallback already charges pv - load, so the flag is a no-op there by construction). Unknown pv or load measurement => INACTIVE (never regulate blind - the economic-guard convention, like the peak guard, the trim and the load following). SAFETY BY ALGEBRA: the raised charge is bounded by the MEASURED surplus, so the predicted grid power load + battery - pv is <= 0 and moves TOWARD zero from the export side - it can never create or raise a grid IMPORT (the §14a import bound and the peak-shaving quarter-hour target are untouched by construction) and it only ever REDUCES export, so the §14a export bound and any feed-in cap hold a fortiori. Because it RAISES a value, the raised target is re-run through the full guard chain (rated band, SoC ceiling, EEG solar-only charge clamp, §14a envelope) - it is never written past a guard, and it can never widen one. It only ever raises a NON-NEGATIVE command: it never turns a commanded discharge into a charge (no direction flip), so it is disjoint from the load-following duty by construction. Absorption is a DELIBERATE correction, not a failed write: the edge writes the raised value, so the register readback matches it and the confirmation logic must never report 'setpoint not adopted' - the edge names the correction on its local card instead.
